if (!/^[0-9a-f]{40,64}$/i.test(sha)) return fail('publication SHA unavailable');
    if (remote.code === 0 && remote.stdout.trim() === `${sha}\t${ref}`)
evidence.reason: Line 38 accepts uppercase hex via the `/i` flag, but line 61 compares the caller's `sha` verbatim against `git ls-remote` output, which emits canonical lowercase object IDs. Git resolves uppercase object IDs for the push and merge-base checks, so a push that succeeds but loses its acknowledgement is misreported as a failure. Lowercasing `sha` for the comparison, or rejecting uppercase in validation, fixes the false negative.
